review_notes: I read the whole file and the ARS `Opposite` definition (CFSG/Timmesfeld/ARS/Defs.lean) to check that the two non-trivial `Opposite` components have the same shape under swapping α and β. I did not look up the exact signatures of `hD.conj`, `hD.fixes` or `hD.regular`. I inferred them from how the proof uses them, and the sketches below assume those shapes. Nothing here was compiled. The code that applies `MulAction.injective` is a plausible replacement, not a tested one. The `hfree` helper, the cardinality bijection and the final assembly are not repeated elsewhere in the file.

findings.excerpt: obtain ⟨b, hbα, -⟩ := hVreg β α (a • β) hαβ haβ
findings.problem: The second and third components of `Opposite` are proved by two nearly identical 15-line blocks with α and β swapped (lines 57–71 and 72–86). Each block does the same four steps. First, `a ≠ 1` gives `a • y ≠ y` via `hfree`. Second, `a • y ≠ x` follows from `a` fixing `x`. Third, regularity of `V y` on Ω∖{y} gives a `b ∈ V y` with `b • x = a • y`. Fourth, `hD.conj b x` and `hD.conj a y` give equality of the conjugated subgroups, and `b ≠ 1` comes from `a • y ≠ x`. A fix or change to one block must be copied by hand into the other.
findings.proposed_change: Inside the proof, before `hopp`, prove one symmetric lemma. `have key : ∀ x y : Ω, x ≠ y → ∀ a ∈ V x, a ≠ 1 → ∃ b ∈ V y, b ≠ 1 ∧ (V x).map (MulAut.conj b).toMonoidHom = (V y).map (MulAut.conj a).toMonoidHom`. Proof sketch: from `hfree x a ha y hxy.symm` get `a • y ≠ y`. From the fixing fact `hVfix x a ha` get `a • y ≠ x`. Then `obtain ⟨b, hb, -⟩ := hVreg y x (a • y) hxy h` gives `b • x = a • y`. Take `b.2`. If `b = 1` then `a • y = x`, which is a contradiction. Finish with `rw [hD.conj b x, hD.conj a y, hb]`. Then `hopp := ⟨fun hVV => …, key α β hαβ, key β α hβα⟩`. The middle component of `hopp` is `key α β hαβ`. The third is `key β α hβα`, which is exactly the required `∀ b ∈ V β, b ≠ 1 → ∃ a ∈ V α, a ≠ 1 ∧ conjSub (V β) a = conjSub (V α) b`. The `V α ≠ V β` component stays as it is. Both uses sit under the hypotheses already in scope (`hfree`, `hVfix`, `hVreg`, `hD.conj`), and no new imports are needed.
findings.benefit: The roughly 30 lines shrink to one lemma of about 12 lines plus two one-line uses. The symmetry argument is stated once, so the reader checks one proof, and maintenance touches one place.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out three times: `haα` (lines 59–65), `hbβ` (74–80) and `hne` (94–100). If `g` fixes `x` and `g • y = x`, then `y = g⁻¹ • g • y = g⁻¹ • x = x`. Each time this is a 3-step `calc` ending in `rw [inv_smul_eq_iff, h5]`, and each time the result is used to show that a point other than `x` is not sent to `x`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a local `have moves : ∀ (g : H) (x y : Ω), g • x = x → y ≠ x → g • y ≠ x := fun g x y hx hy h => hy (MulAction.injective g (h.trans hx.symm))`. Then `haα := moves a α β (hVfix α a ha) hβα`, `hbβ := moves b β α (hVfix β b hb) hαβ` and `hne u := moves u α β (MulAction.mem_stabilizer_iff.mp (hRα u.2)) hβα`. All three uses are under their existing hypotheses (`hVfix`, `hRα`, `hβα`, `hαβ`). This can be combined with the `key` lemma from the other finding, which then needs `moves` only once. The proof relies on `MulAction.injective g`, which I did not check by name in the mathlib sources.
findings.benefit: Three copies of the same group-action argument become one stated fact. Each use site shrinks to a single term that states its intent (the point stays away from x), and the proof is easier to read and to fix.
